label: GO after S2 win when belief favours S2, ramping up over episode trials ~90-99
terms: (phase == GO) * (prev_reward == 1) * (prev_state != 1) * (prev_action != 1) * (belief < 0.3) * np.clip(ep_trial - 88, 0, 15) ;; (phase == GO) * (prev_reward == 1) * (prev_state != 1) * (prev_action != 1) * (belief < 0.3) * np.clip(ep_trial - 92, 0, 15) ;; (phase == GO) * (prev_reward == 1) * (prev_state != 1) * (prev_action != 1) * (belief < 0.3) * np.clip(ep_trial - 95, 0, 15)
explanation: Sparse feature (0.4% of steps), only at GO. Magnitude is driven by: previous trial a2 -> S2 rewarded (or unknown previous state with reward on the window first trial), ideal-observer belief that S2 is good (belief < 0.3), and episode position: near zero before trial ~90, then ramping steeply (~0.3 at t90, ~1.2 at t93, ~1.9 at t99). Expressed as a piecewise-linear ramp in ep_trial gated by the S2-win + S2-belief condition. Dropping the belief gate cuts test R^2 to 0.17; a sigmoid ramp did worse (dev 0.37-0.39). Not helped by: trial-before reward/state, belief_cover, graded belief log-odds, the upcoming choice (action==2, future; no gain), or hidden good state / since_rev (+0.01 dev). Dev R^2 beyond timing 0.60, test 0.38 (test timing baseline differs: 0.05 vs 0.10). The earlier value/policy-based description (low value, strong a2 commitment) is replaced here by belief + episode time with little apparent loss; the profile ceiling for additive cues (all=0.01) is uninformative because the effect is a multiplicative conjunction. Remaining misses are under-predicted streaks of S2 wins late in the episode, whose magnitude exceeds the fitted ramp.
